text:
oliver: Heads up — after the canary of the new route-routing change I'm seeing heavy stuttering in the console charts. Small dashboards ok, but big ones (50+ series) repaint/reflow multiple times on route switch.

sophie: saw this on staging too. grabbing flamegraphs now. my gut: rehydrate + layout thrash on route change.

jay: telemetry matches — big spike in chart.render CPU and bundle.parse right when the route flips. snippet from the sample:
```
metric chart.render 1714300001 850ms
metric bundle.parse 1714300001 120ms
event route.change panels=6
```

oliver: trace link: https://redwood.internal/traces/console/abc123 (contains timeline). looks like repeated measureText calls from axis formatter during each reflow.

sophie: do we still call global cache invalidation on every route change? iirc router had `clearDataCache()` to force fresh queries.

jay: yep — router.ts has `onRouteChange(() => cache.invalidateAll())` which was added for sticky time-range bugs. that is very aggressive.

maria: can we narrow it? invalidate by panel id / queryHash instead of nuking everything. also debounce the invalidation for 200ms to avoid the thrash when multiple route params arrive.

deploy-bot: deploy v2026.03.19-canary-rc3 to console-service succeeded :rocket:

oliver: quick local patch: only invalidate panels with changed queryHash. canary on my env shows ~80% reduction in reflow counts and much smoother paint.

jay: nice. there's a secondary issue: intl polyfill is lazy-imported inside PanelRenderer, so on route switch multiple panels lazy-load the same polyfill chunk causing repeated parse/exec overhead. we should hoist it to a shared singleton or preload for canary.

sophie: agreed. hoisting will avoid per-panel bundle.parse spikes. also let's cap telemetry trace sampling on the canary to 1% — the full-trace traffic is noisy and affects CPU on the client.

maria: i'll open a PR for targeted invalidation + debounce. jay can you take the polyfill hoist? soph will add telemetry cap. i'll coordinate reviews.

oliver: also proposing a small smoke test in canary: load a 100-series chart, measure firstPaint and total reflow count, fail if reflows > 3. catches regressions early.

sophie: and add an e2e assertion that route change doesn't recreate DOM nodes for panels more than once. should prevent accidental unmount/remount loops.

maria: punchlist PRs: #4873 invalidate-by-hash, #4874 hoist-intl-singleton, #4875 telemetry-sample-cap. tagging you all for review.

jay: i'll prototype the hoist today. if we can preload the chunk during initial bundle idle time that might be lowest impact.

oliver: thanks team. @maria @jay once PRs are up i'll flip the canary and run the 100-series smoke a few times. :thumbsup:
